page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top 25% at 2865.09. Multi-core performance falls within the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6531.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, yielding 553.27 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 46.79 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Other operations, such as Redis SET operations at 8.77 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 10.68 GB/sec, also align with average tier performance.

The c2d-standard-8 offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing a qualitative resource density suitable for general-purpose and compute-bound workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized tiers. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility for high-speed local database operations or heavy machine learning training. The instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text and image processing, web serving, and small-scale language model inference, where its strong single-core performance can be leveraged.

It features 4 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng testing, while its multi-core CPU, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average tier. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it provides a cost-effective profile for compute-focused workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is suited for web serving, software compilation, image processing, and moderate database operations.
